paragraphs: Stephen tells the council that the Most High does not dwell in houses made by human hands (Acts 7:48). He doesn't trash the tabernacle or the house Solomon built. He just reminds them what God says: "Heaven is My throne and the earth is My footstool." (Acts 7:49) I love my bakery, friend, but if I ever start thinking my ovens can hold God, somebody please sit me down with a cookie.

Then Stephen says the part that makes the room lose it: "You always resist the Holy Spirit, just as your fathers did." (Acts 7:51) These were people who had the law and knew the whole history, and Stephen says they have not kept the law (Acts 7:53). Having the right things around you is not the same as listening to God, like owning a treadmill and calling yourself a runner. So the question for you and me is simple: is my heart open to Him, or am I just keeping the right stuff nearby?

Now look at Stephen when the council is at its angriest. Before they rush at him, he sees "heaven open and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God" (Acts 7:56), and while they are stoning him, he prays, "Lord, do not hold this sin against them." (Acts 7:60) I think this part is heavy, and Saul is standing right there, giving approval (Acts 8:1), but it shows us that Jesus is not far from His people in their hardest hour, and that He can give us a heart that forgives, even then.
